data.name: Udbhavi
data.gender_notes: Udbhavi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘udbhav’, meaning ‘awakened’ or ‘emerged’. This name symbolizes the idea of new beginnings, growth, and rebirth. In Hindu mythology, Udbhavi is a name for the goddess Lakshmi, who represents prosperity, wealth, and abundance. The name Udbhavi carries the meaning “Awakened, Emerged” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Udbhavi usually hope their child will grow to embody awakened, emerged and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes new beginnings, growth, and rebirth.
data.etymology: Udbhavi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Awakened, Emerged.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Udbhavi total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

In Hinduism, the concept of new beginnings is deeply intertwined with various rituals, festivals, and stories.

historical_references.reference: Udbhavi was the name of a great queen of the Satavahana dynasty, who ruled over the western Deccan region in the 1st century AD. She is known for her military campaigns against the Saka invaders and her patronage of art, especially rock-cut architecture.
historical_references.context: Satavahana Dynasty, Western Deccan, Military campaigns against Sakas, Rock-cut architecture patronage

historical_references.reference: Udbhavi is also the name of a goddess worshipped in South India, particularly in the state of Karnataka. She is believed to be a form of the goddess Parvati, and is associated with the creation and nourishment of life, especially agricultural prosperity. Her cult rose to prominence during the late medieval period, from the 13th to the 16th centuries.
historical_references.context: Goddess Parvati, South India, Agricultural prosperity
